judgements.endpoint: RMSE and correlation of predicted ddG on the Megascale held-out test split for the ThermoMPNN comparison set
limitations: Developer comparison: the authors built ThermoMPNN and chose the comparator set (methods with readily accessible code).
Megascale proteins are 40-72-residue domains, many de novo designed, measured by one proteolysis assay over a narrow ddG range (-3 to 5 kcal/mol).
RaSP and PROSTATA were retrained on Megascale data for this table; other comparators use their published training.
No uncertainty is printed in Table 2 (Table 1 ablations give seed SD for ThermoMPNN only).

evidence_gaps_add: Both mega-scale comparisons are developer papers (ThermoMPNN and ESM therm); no independent comparison on the mega-scale proteolysis set with printed per-method values was found.
No linked comparison includes the AMFR construct of the existing judgements, so the new evidence does not resolve them.
Only Pancotti et al. 2022 tests antisymmetry across many tools; the other two report it partly (Dieckhaus Ssym) or not at all.
No linked comparison reports uncertainty intervals for per-method correlations; Dieckhaus prints seed standard deviations only for its own model in Table 1, which is not transcribed here.
Stability Oracle, PROSTATA and ABYSSAL appear only as values compiled from their own papers (Dieckhaus Table 3), not as reruns.
use_case_changes.exclusions_note: No exclusion change is proposed. The Chu single-protein datasets measure melting temperature, chemical stability or abundance, not ddG of folding, so those seven judgements are proxy; the exclusion on whole-protein function and pathogenicity still holds because none of these endpoints is organismal fitness or a clinical label.
use_case_changes.setting_proposed: Existing AMFR evidence, plus three published comparisons: 21 predictors on S669 with reverse variants (Pancotti et al. 2022); 12 methods on a homology-clustered mega-scale held-out split and a homologue-free FireProtDB split, with compiled Ssym and S669 values (Dieckhaus et al. 2024); and seven methods on held-out mega-scale domains and six larger single-protein stability datasets (Chu et al. 2024).
use_case_changes.decision_proposed: Inspect per-method correlation and error on held-out proteins, the antisymmetry bias, and the drop when moving from small domains to larger proteins, before choosing a method for the intended protein and assay.
use_case_changes.pin_warning: Changing setting or decision alters fields pinned by the three reviewed judgements on this use case, which would be withheld until re-reviewed and re-pinned. Adding links, gaps, sources and citations does not.

summary_proposal.value: Three new comparisons join the existing AMFR evidence. Each uses its own dataset, split and metric, so the numbers cannot be pooled. On S669, 669 experimental ddG variants in proteins unlike the usual training sets (Pancotti et al. 2022), the best Pearson correlation on direct variants was about 0.5 (MAESTRO 0.50, ACDC-NN 0.46) and FoldX reached 0.22. Reversing each variant exposed strong bias in tools not built to be antisymmetric: mCSM fell to 0.22 on reverse variants with a bias of -0.85, while antisymmetric tools such as INPS-Seq kept the same correlation. On held-out proteins from the mega-scale proteolysis set, clustered at 25% identity (Dieckhaus et al. 2024, the ThermoMPNN developers), ThermoMPNN reached Pearson 0.75 and RMSE 0.71 kcal/mol, RaSP 0.71 and Rosetta 0.53 with RMSE 5.18; FoldX had RMSE 3.87. On a homologue-free FireProtDB split ThermoMPNN fell to 0.65. Chu et al. 2024, the ESM therm developers, show the transfer limit directly: on held-out mega-scale domains Spearman was 0.65 for their fine-tuned model, 0.64 for RaSP and ELASPIC-2 and 0.61 for Rosetta, but on six larger single proteins their model dropped to between -0.11 and 0.03 while ELASPIC-2 stayed at 0.47 to 0.58 and a pretrained ESM-2 3B reached 0.53 on one of them. Values are as printed. None of these comparisons covers the AMFR construct in the existing judgements, and none establishes whole-protein function, fitness or pathogenicity.
summary_proposal.source_locator: Pancotti et al. 2022 Table 1; Dieckhaus et al. 2024 Tables 2-3; Chu et al. 2024 Tables 1-2
summary_proposal.note: The ELASPIC-2 range 0.47 to 0.58 covers its six larger-protein rows; the ESM therm range -0.11 to 0.03 covers the same six. The mCSM bias -0.85 and reverse r 0.22 are from Pancotti Table 1.

concerns_for_reviewer.locator: Table 3 row 'ACDC-NN ( 30 , 36 )' versus Pancotti et al. 2022 Table 1
concerns_for_reviewer.message: Dieckhaus Table 3 prints ACDC-NN S669 RMSE 1.60 and PCC 0.46, citing Pancotti et al. 2022; Pancotti Table 1 prints RMSE 1.49 for direct variants with the same PCC 0.46. Both values are stored, each against its own source.

Rows marked * in Table 2 may be inflated by training-set homologues; in Table 3 the marks mean something different (ThermoMPNN trained on a filtered set; ABYSSAL scored on 420 of 669 variants). Both are recorded on the affected results as source_warnings.
Predictor versions and server access dates are only in the Supplementary Materials, which were not read; configuration versions are therefore unextracted.
Every method is scored on point mutations only, except the authors' own model on the mega-scale set, which also saw multi-point variants. The comparison on that row is therefore not exactly matched.
MAESTRO has the highest direct-variant correlation (0.50) but a bias of -0.57 and reverse correlation 0.20, so ranking by direct correlation alone would mislead.
